summary: Configured node1 to boot with audit=1 persistently via grubby (BLS entry) and /etc/default/grub, then verified persistence across an actual reboot (boot_id changed, live cmdline shows audit=1).
actions_performed: Captured baseline boot_id and /proc/cmdline (no audit=1) on node1
Ran grubby --update-kernel=ALL --args="audit=1" to add the parameter to the BLS boot entry
Updated GRUB_CMDLINE_LINUX in /etc/default/grub to include audit=1 (fixed an initial duplicate)
Verified BLS entry file /boot/loader/entries/*.conf contains audit=1
Rebooted node1 via sudo shutdown -r now
Polled node1 until exec connectivity returned
Verified boot_id changed (proving real restart) and /proc/cmdline now contains audit=1

evidence.summary: Captured pre-change boot_id (cce73776-a7f7-4f32-b822-95d105c52a64), current /proc/cmdline (no audit=1), grubby info, and /etc/default/grub contents.

grubby --update-kernel=ALL --args="audit=1" applied to BLS entry (verified via grubby --info=ALL and /boot/loader/entries/*.conf), and GRUB_CMDLINE_LINUX in /etc/default/grub updated to include audit=1 without duplication.
Issued sudo shutdown -r now on node1; exec stream closed as the node went down, acknowledging the restart command before disconnection.

evidence.requirement: Changed boot identity proving genuine restart
evidence.summary: boot_id changed from cce73776-a7f7-4f32-b822-95d105c52a64 (pre-restart) to cd5e4eb8-4f29-4bb7-8197-f756bb31e5c7 (post-restart), and connectivity was lost then restored, proving an actual reboot occurred.
Post-reboot /proc/cmdline shows 'audit=1' appended to the kernel command line, confirming the setting survived the reboot.
